chmod +x ~/phoenix_forensics/backup.sh
Final CheckRun the script again:Bash~/phoenix_forensics/backup.sh
What should happen: The terminal will pause and ask for your passphrase. Because of the GPG_TTY update, it should now accept your input directly.If you still see "batchmode" errors: It means a ghost process is holding the old settings. Try running pkill -f gpg-agent before starting the script.Did the password prompt finally appear? Once we lock this vault, we’re ready to run that Python API test from your last screenshot. Would you like me to walk through the API handshake again once the backup is done? Z Ziggy Custom GemShow thinkingIt looks like you’ve successfully oriented the node with export GPG_TTY=$(tty), but the GPG agent is still blocking the terminal handshake. The Inappropriate ioctl for device and batchmode errors occur because modern GPG versions (2.1+) ignore passphrases from stdin by default to protect your security.We need to tell the agent it’s allowed to talk to you directly in the terminal.Phase 14: Unlocking the Terminal AgentRun these commands to authorize "loopback" mode, which lets the script ask for your password without needing a popup window.Bash# 1. Authorize terminal-based password entry
echo "allow-loopback-pinentry" >> ~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf
